title: Criminal Code Amendment (Misrepresentation of Age to a Minor) Bill 2013
short_title: Criminal Code Amendment (Misrepresentation of Age to a Minor) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create offences for adults who lie about their age in online messages to children to arrange a meeting or commit another offence.
It would cover senders over 18 communicating with recipients under 16, with imprisonment penalties of five years for encouraging meetings and eight for other offences.
The offences would also cover fictitious recipients used in undercover operations, with defences concerning the recipient’s age and reasonable conduct by specified officers.
changes: Courts could consider appearance, medical opinions and official records when determining a person’s age.
A defendant relying on a belief that the recipient was at least 16 would carry an evidential burden.
The amendments would begin the day after Royal Assent.
summary.affected: Adult online message senders, children under 16 and law enforcement, intelligence and security officers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Helen Kroger
speeches.brief: The Selection of Bills Committee presented its 11th report of 2013, recommending six bills be referred to specific committees for inquiry with set reporting dates, including the Environment Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 (report by 12 February 2014) and the Criminal Code Amendment (Harming Australians) Bill 2013 (report by 4 March 2014).
